profile.name: Wolosso
profile.tagline: West African popular dance marked by isolated, rolling hip movement
profile.insight: Emerging in Ivory Coast in 2006, Wolosso's undulating hip circles sparked controversy across West Africa, turning its name into a cultural shorthand for provocative lifestyle.
profile.profile: Wolosso is a modern popular dance that originated in Ivory Coast in 2006 and spread across West Africa. The movement is defined by isolated, circular hip rotations and intermittent lowering of the torso, placing heavy visual emphasis on the buttocks. Performed to an offbeat-accented 4/4 meter at tempos between 40 and 70 beats per minute, the style synthesizes traditional African folk idioms with global pop dance aesthetics. Beyond the dance floor, the term evolved across the region to signify provocative attire and unconventional social attitudes.
profile.profile_long:
Wolosso originated in Ivory Coast in 2006 as a popular dance fad before circulating widely across West Africa. The form took shape as an energetic synthesis of indigenous African folk dances and contemporary urban pop movement. By translating rural and traditional body language into a commercial nightlife context, Wolosso captured the attention of youth cultures across national borders.

The dance is characterized by isolated, rolling hip circles executed while maintaining strong bodily control. During these circular pelvic rotations, dancers—particularly women—periodically lower their torsos forward, bringing pronounced visual prominence to the rear. The footwork and spatial formations, though uncodified in formal manuals, support an upright yet dynamic pelvic articulation that directly mirrors the underlying syncopation.

Wolosso is danced to an offbeat-accented 4/4 meter, operating at measured tempos between 40 and 70 beats per minute. This rhythmic foundation is frequently overlaid with polyrhythmic counters typical of African music traditions. The musical style is driven by modern urban West African production, incorporating vocal arrangements whose explicit thematic content has drawn sharp public debate.

The social setting of Wolosso is firmly rooted in modern clubs, dance halls, and urban streets rather than ceremonial clearings. Its emergence generated significant controversy, particularly in predominantly Muslim societies across the region, where the explicit pelvic movements were deemed provocative or offensive. Detached from their historical and ritual environments, these folk-derived articulations became associated with decadent Western influences. Eventually, the word 'Wolosso' transitioned beyond choreography to become a broader cultural shorthand denoting revealing dress and an unapologetically free lifestyle.

sections.origins_and_history: Wolosso arose in 2006 in Ivory Coast as a popular dance style that rapidly spread throughout West Africa. Historically, the style represents a synthesis of traditional African folk dances and Western pop dance culture.
sections.how_it_is_danced: The dance is performed through isolated circular hip movements. Female dancers periodically lower the upper body, placing heavy emphasis on the buttocks. The movement operates over an offbeat-accented 4/4 meter, at moderate to fast musical pacing between 40 and 70 bpm.
sections.music_and_instruments: The dance relies on an offbeat-emphasized 4/4 rhythm that is often layered with polyrhythmic counters typical of African folk traditions. The musical tempo is positioned between 40 and 70 bpm. Various Wolosso musicians have faced criticism for incorporating sexually explicit lyrical content.
sections.costume_and_setting: Wolosso belongs to contemporary urban popular culture and secular social dancing. Over time, the term broadened to designate revealing, permissive styles of dress and unconventional lifestyles, especially among women.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: The dance functions as a contemporary social dance. In predominantly Muslim countries of West Africa, Wolosso has stirred strong public offense due to movements perceived as lascivious. Stripped of their original ritual and folk contexts, these bodily articulations are frequently identified with decadent Western culture.
sections.lineage: Wolosso descends from a fusion of historical African folk dances and modern Western popular dance trends.

basic_steps: Stand with knees softly bent to prepare for pelvic isolation
Engage an offbeat rhythm in 4/4 meter
Execute continuous, isolated circular movements of the hips
Lower the torso forward while maintaining the rolling hip circles to emphasize the buttocks
Return the torso upright while keeping the circular pelvic rhythm uninterrupted

episode_brief.title_hook: The Beat That Shook the Street
episode_brief.logline: Born in 2006 Abidjan, Wolosso turned traditional hip isolations into a regional dance explosion and a lightning rod for cultural debate.

lesson_ladder.goal: Establish the 4/4 offbeat weight shift and knee flexion
drills: Count the 4/4 pulse highlighting the offbeats at 55 bpm
Knee softening and weight transfer drill without pelvic rotation
Standing stationary hip isolations left and right

lesson_ladder.goal: Execute continuous circular hip rotation in time
drills: Four-point pelvic compass isolation (front, right, back, left)
Smoothing the four points into a continuous rolling circle
Sustaining the roll across eight consecutive 4/4 bars

lesson_ladder.goal: Lower the upper body forward while sustaining the hip rotation
drills: Hinging the upper body forward 45 degrees with a neutral spine
Initiating the hip roll from the hinged torso position
Transitioning dynamically between upright and lowered torso during continuous rolls

Contrasting modern urban club dance with rural folk origins

claims.text: Wolosso is a fad dance that originated in Ivory Coast in 2006 and spread throughout West Africa.
claims.quote: Wolosso ist ein Modetanz, der 2006 in der Elfenbeinküste entstanden ist und sich seitdem in ganz Westafrika ausbreitet.

claims.text: The dance is defined by isolated circular hip movements and periodic lowering of the upper body.
claims.quote: Charakteristisch für diesen Tanz sind isoliert kreisende Hüftbewegungen, bei – zumindest bei den weiblichen Tänzern – zeitweise erfolgendem Absenken des Oberkörpers

claims.text: The dance strongly emphasizes the buttocks.
claims.quote: sodass das Gesäß stark betont wird.

claims.text: The rhythm is an offbeat-accented 4/4 meter that can be layered with other rhythms.
claims.quote: Als Rhythmus wird ein Offbeat-betonter 4/4-Takt bevorzugt, der gelegentlich – wie in der afrikanischen Volksmusik üblich – durch andere Rhythmen überlagert wird.

claims.text: The tempo ranges between 40 and 70 beats per minute.
claims.quote: Das Tempo ist mäßig bis schnell, zwischen 40 und 70 bpm.

claims.text: Historically, the dance is a synthesis of African folk dances and Western pop culture fads.
claims.quote: Historisch ist der Tanz als eine Synthese von afrikanischen Volkstänzen und Modetänzen der westlichen Popkultur erkennbar.

claims.text: The dance caused public offense in predominantly Muslim countries due to its hip movements.
claims.quote: In überwiegend muslimisch geprägten Ländern erregt der Wolosso wegen seiner als lasziv empfundenen Hüftschwünge häufig Anstoß.

claims.text: The term Wolosso has expanded into a synonym for a revealing dress code and permissive lifestyle, particularly among women.
claims.quote: Mittlerweile hat sich die Bedeutung von „Wolosso“ erweitert, als Synonym für einen freizügigen Kleidungs- und Lebensstil, insbesondere von Frauen.
